findings.title: The 135s real-time heartbeat regression is genuinely flaky — I reproduced a failure twice on this head, including in isolation
findings.detail: UPGRADED FROM MARGIN-ANALYSIS TO OBSERVED FAILURE. Running `pnpm --filter flywheel-voice-codex test:run` at this head failed (exit 1, 135.57s), and re-running the single file in isolation failed again: `AssertionError: expected 1 to be greater than or equal to 2` at :75 (`expect(heartbeats.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2)`). My earlier rounds predicted the `successes >= 26` assertion as the risk; the real binding constraint is tighter. Mechanism: successes are enqueued on the 20s aggregate cadence, so heartbeats (DEFAULT_SUCCESS_LOG_HEARTBEAT_MS = 60_000) land at roughly t+60s and t+120s inside a RUN_FOR_MS = 135_000 window. Once per-iteration drift pushes the 20s enqueue points out by ~15%, the second heartbeat falls past 135s and only one is emitted. Both of my failures were on a loaded machine, which is exactly the CI condition — `Unit (light)` runs with VITEST_MAX_FORKS=1 on a shared ubuntu runner. Honest counter-evidence: this test passed on CI at the two previous heads and passed locally three times in rounds 3-5, so it is intermittent, not deterministic. This is test-only (no product code is implicated), but it will intermittently red a required job. Deriving the expected heartbeat count from measured elapsed time, or extending RUN_FOR_MS past 2x the heartbeat interval with margin, removes the risk.

findings.title: One unexpected file in the pending spool directory permanently disables the entire daemon-side health reporter across every restart
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred to follow-ups). censusSafeFiles throws on ANY directory entry not matching ^[a-f0-9]{64}\.json$ (:1092). writeAtomic creates its scratch file as `.${randomUUID()}.tmp` in that same directory (:995) and removes it only in a finally block, so a SIGKILL between open and rm leaves a permanent non-matching entry; a .DS_Store does the same. loadPendingSpools catches, calls signalUnavailable and returns false, setting filesystemBlocked (:338-340) — which runs exactly once per process behind the replayLoaded guard. Consequences compound: registerBoot returns false at :342-345 BEFORE startWatchdog(), so there is no 60s evaluate watchdog and no maintenance checkpoint for the process lifetime; queueAvailable() short-circuits at :776 so no observation is ever queued; and cli.ts:139 discards the boolean. The only evidence is one console.error line (cli.ts:117-121). After an ordinary crash the daemon runs for days emitting zero health data and never self-heals on restart. Restrict the census to the expected filename set (ignore or clean unmatched entries) instead of failing the whole load.

findings.title: record_startup opens an episode only if demand_state is 'required' at that instant, and the duplicate short-circuit prevents re-evaluation
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). record_startup bumps phase='startup_failed', failure_count and operation='startup' even when demand is not 'required', but opens no episode and mints no intent, while still inserting the startup_events row — so every later call with the same stable startupAttemptId (= session.sessionId, voice-health-projector.ts:836) returns duplicate and re-evaluates nothing. Trigger: record-demand failing across the startup window leaves demand_state at 'none'; note the new fail-closed path also parks demand_state at 'unknown', which is likewise not 'required'. Result: no Discord alert and no incident for a session that never goes live, and since a 'desired' row is never swept by sweepVoiceSessions there is no later failed transition to re-open it.

findings.title: no_action() inserts the producer_events row, so a recovery observation is consumed permanently and its incident can never be cleared
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). Previously reproduced end-to-end: demand required with identity (m1,s1); session_failed(m1,s1) opens a session_unavailable episode with a pending intent; session_recovered(m1 -> successor s2) arriving while the snapshot still lists s1 returns 'no_action' and burns its producerEventSeq; after the Bridge publishes s2, retrying the identical event returns 'duplicate' with no effect, leaving the episode OPEN and the intent 'pending'. health.ts:665-688 accepts 'no_action' and splices the event out of its spool document, so the daemon never retries it either. The pure race is narrow, but it widens whenever demand_state is not 'required' — including the new fail-closed 'unknown' window.

findings.title: A session_ended event writes last_iteration_success_at and success_count, the poll-scope success markers
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). UPDATE health SET phase='session_ended', last_iteration_success_at = ?, last_progress_at = ?, success_count = success_count + 1 ... driven by a session-scope observation. Plan section 3 requires session recovery to write an independent sessionRecoveryProof '而不是伪造lastIterationSuccessAt', and the session_recovered branch correctly touches only last_progress_at. The fixed page can show '最近完整成功: <now>' while the poll dependency has never succeeded and its poll_dependency episode is still open, and the heartbeat_stale anchor in evaluate_health's idle branch is reset by an event that proves nothing about the desired poll. Note this is now the only remaining path by which a non-poll event moves a poll-scope marker: the sibling defect in the `progress` branch was fixed this round.

findings.title: evaluate_health has no staleness branch for starting / session_ended / session_failed / dormant / stopped
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). Only failed_retrying, idle and active are evaluated; every other phase falls to 'else: return response' (no_action) at any horizon. Combined with voice-health-projector.ts mapping phase==='session_ended' unconditionally to status 'healthy', a daemon that freezes in one of those phases produces no local staleness evidence whatsoever. The backstop is the Bridge-side startup guard, which this round was tightened but still only covers provisioning/desired/claimed/warming rows. Plan section 3: '首启无记录有60秒宽限，缺字段为unknown，不为健康' — there is no expiry of that grace.

findings.title: No retention anywhere in the source store, and the 20s demand refresh appends a change row indefinitely
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred), and this round's F1 fix slightly sharpens it: now that voice-session-runtime.ts stamps a fresh Bridge observation clock on every refresh, the 20s change rows are no longer byte-identical, so the projection payload genuinely changes every 20s and applyVoiceHealthProjection reports changed=true on every projector run — requestRefresh('flywheel','voice_health_changed') fires every 60s indefinitely (bounded by the refresher's 5s debounce and coalescing to one regeneration+publish per minute, and currently skipped for Linear-unbound projects). Volume is unchanged at ~3 rows/min, ~4300/day, each a full projection snapshot of ~1-2KB, and voice-health.py still contains no DELETE for changes / producer_events / notification_attempts / demand_transition_events / startup_events, with wal_autocheckpoint=0 and checkpoint=False on the hot path (~6MB/day steady state). Plan section 3 assumes retention exists.

findings.title: A curl transport failure (exit 6/7, provably nothing sent) is collapsed to delivery_unknown, which is never retried and never re-minted
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). voice_post_discord's exit status is discarded into VOICE_HTTP_CODE='000' and routed to record_voice_source_delivery delivery_unknown. delivery_unknown is absent from CLAIMABLE_STATES (voice-health.py:85) and from retryableIntentIds (voice-health-projector.ts), and _open_episode returns the existing episode's existing intent while the episode stays open, so no new intent is minted. No meta-alert fires, and the receipt matches SAFE_ALERT_RECEIPT so the Bridge does not even log. Failure: the host's network drops — exactly the condition that opens the episode — curl exits 7 and the alert is lost for the whole episode. Plan section 4 draws the line at '明确未发送/429可以按既有队列重试'; curl exit 6/7 is 明确未发送 and the evidence is discarded.

findings.title: Bootstrap startup-spool events are imported only when there is exactly one demand identity
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). readStartupEvents() is invoked only under demandState==='required' && sourceStatus==='available' && identities.length === 1. With zero or two-or-more concurrent voice demands — and now also during the new fail-closed window, which forces identities to [] — wrapper-level startup failures are never imported, never alerted and never archived. The writer caps the spool at 128 files / 1MB and the overflow is swallowed by '|| true', so once saturated, later startup failures are dropped with only stderr. Plan section 4's bootstrap path expects unconditional import keyed on the Bridge's own demand association. Separately, spool/consumed/ has no pruning owner.

findings.title: createVoiceHealthStartupSpoolReader() is constructed with no root while every sibling in the same call gets FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR, so an isolated Bridge reads and can consume the host's production spool
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). plugin.ts:7215 computes voiceHealthStateRoot from FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR?.trim() || ~/.flywheel and passes it to readExport and the guard; three lines later readStartupEvents: createVoiceHealthStartupSpoolReader() is called with no argument and the reader resolves join(input.homeDir ?? homedir(), '.flywheel', 'voice-startup-spool'), never consulting FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR. scripts/test-deploy.sh:1598 gives a 529 slot Bridge FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR=${state} with no HOME override, so a slot Bridge reads the founder's real spool on every tick. If that slot's own store reports required demand with exactly one identity it wins the .consumer.lock flock, records the production startup failure into the SLOT's health DB, and renames the production document into consumed/ — after which the production Bridge never mints the intent. Honest boundary: the cross-root read is unconditional and certain; the consume branch is reachable but I could not construct a slot run that reaches it, and evidence is archived rather than deleted. The homeDir parameter already exists and is used by the reader's own test.

findings.title: validateExport's `currentProjection === undefined` guard does not catch the helper's JSON null, so a source with no health row fails every tick
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). Probed against a virgin state root: export returns "currentProjection":null (voice-health.py _current_projection returns None when the health row is absent). validateExport's check `(!raw.hasMore && raw.currentProjection === undefined)` uses strict equality so null passes, then record(exported.currentProjection, ...) throws in BOTH projectView and the Bridge guard — the latter BEFORE the startup_not_ready waiting block. The projector then throws, marks the projection unavailable, logs every tick, and the guard plus the startup-spool import never run. It normally self-heals because record-demand creates the health row (confirmed by probe) and VoiceSessionRuntime.start() fires before the awaited startup tick, so the practical exposure is the startup race plus any host where record-demand can never succeed.

findings.title: pause() never detaches its abort listener on the timer path, while this PR feeds it a long-lived AbortSignal on every idle poll
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). pause() registers signal.addEventListener('abort', fn, {once:true}) and returns on the timer path WITHOUT removeEventListener; {once:true} only detaches after the event fires, and abort fires once at shutdown. This PR introduced the exposure: pre-PR daemon.ts called options.sleep(idlePollMs) with NO signal (verified against e82193650:daemon.ts:244,309), whereas run() now passes this.sleepController.signal — one AbortController per daemon (daemon.ts:302) — at daemon.ts:326 and :348, and cli.ts:357 wires sleep: pause. One listener is permanently retained per idle poll: 12/min at the FLYWHEEL_VOICE_IDLE_POLL_MS default of 5000, ~17k/day. I verified Node emits NO MaxListenersExceededWarning for AbortSignal at 40 listeners, so the growth is silent. One removeEventListener in the timer path closes it.

findings.title: claim/renew install the lease from an unvalidated body.leaseTtlMs, so a malformed 2xx produces a NaN deadline that never fences plus a 1ms timer spin
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). This PR rewrote the request layer specifically so a 2xx is not assumed successful and added strict decoding for /desired, but claim (:306), renew (:332) and renewRecovered (:352) still pass body.leaseTtlMs straight into VoiceLease.install, whose only typing is a compile-time generic on a network response. With leaseTtlMs absent or non-numeric, deadlineMs = sentAt + NaN - timeout = NaN (:105); VoiceLease.assert() then evaluates `!active || monoNow() >= NaN` = false and never throws, so the fence that stops two daemons from both believing they hold authority is silently disabled for the session. SessionLifetime.armDeadline re-arms with lease.remainingMs = NaN, which Node coerces to a 1ms delay, producing a ~1000/s re-arm spin. A Number.isSafeInteger guard in install() closes both.

findings.title: record_delivery has no post-timeout idempotency key, so a worker cannot confirm its own committed write
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). The authorization side is sound — 'sent' requires a matching claim_token, matching binding_digest, intent['channel_id'] == channel_id and snowflake-validated ids, so no fabricated success — but the UPDATE clears claim_token, claimed_at and claim_expires_at. A retry after a 500ms execFile timeout that actually committed returns notification_claim_mismatch, indistinguishable from a genuinely wrong claim. Plan section 3 requires '超时后不能假设未提交：用 ... 重试查询去重记录'. Every other mutating command has such a key.

findings.title: voice_health_demand_events is retention-protected forever while the consuming cursor is in-memory, so Bridge restarts replay the whole history
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). scripts/lib/fly-2006-retention-tables/teamlead/voice_health_demand_events.json classifies the table protectedCurrentOrReference, which fly-2006-retention-loader.mjs treats as a non-delete category — so the append-only trigger log in the shared production teamlead DB grows one row per voice_sessions insert/delete/state/reason/cancel/ending/ended change, forever. demandCursor is a plain in-memory field reset to 0 on every Bridge restart, and projectVoiceDemand drains one 200-event page per 3s tick, so catch-up costs N/200 x 3s. Mitigated this round: because observedAt is now the Bridge clock rather than a data timestamp, demand_observed_at no longer freezes during catch-up, so the fixed page no longer reads stale for the whole replay window — the unbounded growth and linear catch-up remain.

findings.title: demandEvent() drops cancelRequested / endingStarted / previousState, so the helper cannot tell a cancelled demand from a dependency failure
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). The trigger records cancel_requested, ending_started, ended and old_state (StateStore.ts:2810-2859) precisely so the helper can distinguish 'user cancelled' from 'system failed it', but the recorder forwards only eventSeq/eventKind/demandId/attemptId/observedAt (+reasonClass for 'failed'). Failure: a founder cancels a meeting, the session goes ending then times out, and voiceHealthReasonClass maps ending_timeout to session_runtime_failed — the helper opens a session_unavailable incident and pages the engineering channel for a user-initiated cancel. Plan section 3 (防止失败后自动消警) requires the cancel fact to be carried into the record.

findings.title: claim/setState/outbound/receipt failures propagate to the poll path and are recorded as poll_dependency, which a later idle_success closes
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). runOnce() lets bridge.claim() and the lifetime bridge calls throw out to run()'s catch, where pollFailure() records kind:'poll_failed' carrying the diagnostic's operation (claim/state/outbound/receipt). voice-health.py opens a poll_dependency episode for those, and _close_poll_episode closes it on the next idle_success — so a failure to join the room is cleared by an unrelated idle poll, the scope-isolation outcome plan section 3 forbids. Partially mitigated because the demand path independently opens session_unavailable on required->failed and the startup guard covers 'desired' sessions, so this is noise plus premature recovery rather than total blindness.

findings.title: A failure to report the terminal session state to the Bridge is swallowed with no health observation
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). Both terminal paths wrap bridge.setState in try/catch, set terminalConfirmed=false and only console.error('[voice] session terminal receipt unavailable; recovery state retained'). Before this change the error propagated out of runOnce and was counted by run()'s catch. Now the Bridge round-trip failure produces no poll_failed and no session_failed observation, no episode and no alert — a whole class of bridge_* failures on the terminal path is invisible to the ledger this change exists to build. recover() (daemon.ts:365-413) likewise emits no health observation on the equivalent path.

findings.title: config_error and invalid receipts retry every 30s forever with no cap, no backoff and no dead-letter transition
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). VoiceHealthAlertDispatcher.drain treats config_error and any unparsable receipt as a retry and calls scheduleRetry with a fixed 30s delay, unbounded. lead-alert.sh returns config_error for permanent conditions (missing helper, failed route preflight, invalid frozen payload), so a misconfigured route spawns /bin/bash lead-alert.sh every 30s for the daemon's lifetime; the Bridge does the same every 60s. claim_notification increments attempt_count but nothing enforces a limit or a dead_lettered transition. meta-alert.sh's 10-minute per-reason debounce bounds the alert noise, but not the process churn or the growing attempt_count.

findings.title: The new 60s+60s leased-startup bound can fire startup_not_ready while a session is still legitimately inside its 120s founder-presence grace
findings.detail: NEW this round, arising from the (correct) fix to warming-lease-suppresses-startup-guard. The guard now excuses a leased claimed/warming session only while now - createdAt < STARTUP_NOT_READY_MS + LEASED_STARTUP_GRACE_MS = 120s. But the daemon's own legitimate wait is presenceGraceMs, default 120_000 (config.ts:161), and it begins only after desired->claim->setState warming->session.start(), i.e. roughly createdAt+5..25s — so waitForFounder can legitimately run until createdAt+125..145s. A founder who joins the voice channel more than ~110s after the session row is created therefore gets a session_unavailable / startup_not_ready incident and a Discord alert for a system that then works. It self-heals (the same session reaching live+renew emits session_recovered, which matches the current identity and closes the episode since liveAt > openedAt), so the cost is alert noise rather than a stuck incident, and the chosen bound is already twice as lenient as the plan's stated 60s boundary. Consider deriving the grace from presenceGraceMs, or anchoring the boundary on the desired->claimed transition rather than createdAt.

findings.title: _restore_demand_marker restores source_status but not the demand_source_unavailable reason_class that idle_success nulls out
findings.detail: NEW this round; a small residual in the otherwise-correct fix to result-write-erases-demand-source-unavailable. Verified against the real helper: after a fail-closed record-demand (trigger_invalid) the row reads {demandState: unknown, sourceStatus: unavailable, reasonClass: demand_source_unavailable}; after one ordinary idle_success it reads {demandState: unknown, sourceStatus: unavailable, reasonClass: None}. The two fields the projector actually derives status from (sourceStatus, demandState) are now correctly preserved — which is why the page behaviour is right — but the recorded fault class is still erased by idle_success's `reason_class = NULL`, so the health row loses the diagnostic that says WHY the source is unavailable. Restoring reason_class alongside source_status in _restore_demand_marker would make the marker whole.

findings.title: The voice-health tick is the only projector awaited ahead of gatePoller.start(); bounded, but an unnecessary boot dependency
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). Bounded and not a real availability risk, per measurement. Ceiling is ~265 sequential helper calls (two drains of <=32 pages, 1 evaluate, <=128 spool record-startup, <=8 waiting record-startup), each capped by execFile timeout: 500 plus <=128 lock acquisitions at readyTimeoutMs: 500 — but that requires all 265 calls to SUCCEED just under 500ms, since any rejection short-circuits run(). No hang risk: voice-health.py has zero hits for subprocess|Popen|os.system|os.fork. Measured ~45ms/call, so a typical boot is ~0.15s and a full 128-event spool ~6-12s. Flagged only because the two sibling projectors constructed just above live solely in the async 3s poller, whose rejections GatePoller already catches and logs; dropping the pre-start await costs at most one poll cycle of freshness.

findings.title: The TypeScript route/bindingDigest module has zero production importers
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). A repo-wide grep for 'voice-health-alert-route' outside dist finds exactly one importer: packages/teamlead/src/__tests__/voice-health-alert-delivery.test.ts. Production route resolution happens entirely in scripts/lead-alert.sh via node scripts/shuttle-route-bindings.mjs, and the bindingDigest persisted and revalidated by the helper comes from that shell path — not from resolveVoiceHealthAlertRoute, which computes a different digest. The repo carries two independent definitions of the same contract, only one of which ships. Coverage of the shipped path is not missing (scripts/__tests__/voice-health-alert-route.test.sh exercises the real shell sender and passes), so the cost is drift risk plus a TS test that looks like production routing coverage but is not.

findings.title: main() reads stdin unconditionally for every subcommand, so any caller that does not close stdin hangs forever with no deadline
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred as 已记录). `payload = _read_payload()` runs before the command dispatch, so even `init` — which then requires the payload to be None or {} — blocks on an open stdin. PROVEN: `timeout 4 python3 scripts/lib/voice-health.py --state-root $TMP init < <(sleep 30)` exits 124 (hung), while the same command with `</dev/null` exits 0. The helper has no internal deadline. Production callers are safe (the TS clients call child.stdin.end() and bound with timeout: 500; lead-alert.sh pipes via printf which closes stdin), but this already cost the implementer debugging time on macOS, and any future runbook, cron or QA script invoking the helper without redirecting stdin will hang indefinitely. Read stdin only for the commands that take a payload, or only when it is not a TTY.

findings.title: reportFatalStartupFailure discards the error entirely, leaving zero diagnostic for a daemon that will not start
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). The parameter is named _error and the log line is the constant '[voice] fatal reasonClass=startup_not_ready operation=startup'; the spool record carries only the reasonClass. This follows plan section 3's rule that raw Error.message must not reach stderr, and package-onboard-smoke.test.sh asserts the exact string. The cost is that 'voice will not start' — the originating FLY-2693 symptom — produces no locally recoverable detail anywhere. A bounded closed-vocabulary classifier (e.g. mapping the known config errors to startup_config_invalid) would keep the sanitization and restore triage.

findings.title: validateVoiceBridgeUrl hard-fails any non-loopback BRIDGE_URL with no allowlist
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). loadVoiceDaemonConfig throws voice_bridge_url_invalid for any host that is not localhost, [::1] or 127.x.x.x, which the wrapper turns into voice_config_invalid and exit 0. Plan section 2 said '生产默认loopback' and '跨主机部署如存在，按现有可信配置明确allowlist'; no allowlist was implemented, so this is an unannounced hard break for any host configuring a non-loopback Bridge. ::ffff:127.0.0.1 is also unmatched.

findings.title: The voice alert lane silently inherits SHUTTLE_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE as a permission-preflight override
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). VOICE_HEALTH_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE:-${SHUTTLE_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE:-} means a stale or leaked SHUTTLE_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE in the environment also replaces the real Discord VIEW_CHANNEL/SEND_MESSAGES preflight for voice alerts (shuttle-route-bindings.mjs:301-309). A QA harness that exports it and forgets to unset it downgrades a second production lane's sender check with no signal.

findings.title: The frozen-payload openedAt gate is prefix-only while every sibling field is fully anchored
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T") has no end anchor, and the value is interpolated into the Discord BODY. Not exploitable today — the writer validates via _parse_timestamp, jq -n --arg prevents payload injection, and allowed_mentions:{parse:[]} blocks pings — but it is the one unanchored field in an otherwise closed-vocabulary gate. Related latent fragility: jq errors with exit 5 on `null | test(...)`, so any _open_episode call site leaving health.operation NULL would make its alert permanently undeliverable; I re-checked the call sites and each sets operation first, so this is latent only.

findings.title: The demand digest omits project_name and meeting_id, and neither column is in the trigger's UPDATE OF list
findings.detail: NOT FIXED, and deliberate per follow-ups.md ('无关字段更新不改变 revision/digest'). Recording the residual consequence: digestRows carries session_id/state/cancel/ending/ended/reasonClass while demandIdentities also carries projectId and meetingId, and voice_health_demand_sessions_update fires only on state, reason, cancel_requested_at, ending_started_at, ended_at — so an identity-only change (e.g. meeting_id backfilled) produces no event and no digest change, and the helper keeps stale identities, which record_result's session_failed path uses for identity_matches.

advisories.title: A session_ended event writes last_iteration_success_at and success_count, the poll-scope success markers
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). UPDATE health SET phase='session_ended', last_iteration_success_at = ?, last_progress_at = ?, success_count = success_count + 1 ... driven by a session-scope observation. Plan section 3 requires session recovery to write an independent sessionRecoveryProof '而不是伪造lastIterationSuccessAt', and the session_recovered branch correctly touches only last_progress_at. The fixed page can show '最近完整成功: <now>' while the poll dependency has never succeeded and its poll_dependency episode is still open, and the heartbeat_stale anchor in evaluate_health's idle branch is reset by an event that proves nothing about the desired poll. Note this is now the only remaining path by which a non-poll event moves a poll-scope marker: the sibling defect in the `progress` branch was fixed this round.

advisories.title: evaluate_health has no staleness branch for starting / session_ended / session_failed / dormant / stopped
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). Only failed_retrying, idle and active are evaluated; every other phase falls to 'else: return response' (no_action) at any horizon. Combined with voice-health-projector.ts mapping phase==='session_ended' unconditionally to status 'healthy', a daemon that freezes in one of those phases produces no local staleness evidence whatsoever. The backstop is the Bridge-side startup guard, which this round was tightened but still only covers provisioning/desired/claimed/warming rows. Plan section 3: '首启无记录有60秒宽限，缺字段为unknown，不为健康' — there is no expiry of that grace.

advisories.title: No retention anywhere in the source store, and the 20s demand refresh appends a change row indefinitely
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred), and this round's F1 fix slightly sharpens it: now that voice-session-runtime.ts stamps a fresh Bridge observation clock on every refresh, the 20s change rows are no longer byte-identical, so the projection payload genuinely changes every 20s and applyVoiceHealthProjection reports changed=true on every projector run — requestRefresh('flywheel','voice_health_changed') fires every 60s indefinitely (bounded by the refresher's 5s debounce and coalescing to one regeneration+publish per minute, and currently skipped for Linear-unbound projects). Volume is unchanged at ~3 rows/min, ~4300/day, each a full projection snapshot of ~1-2KB, and voice-health.py still contains no DELETE for changes / producer_events / notification_attempts / demand_transition_events / startup_events, with wal_autocheckpoint=0 and checkpoint=False on the hot path (~6MB/day steady state). Plan section 3 assumes retention exists.

advisories.title: A curl transport failure (exit 6/7, provably nothing sent) is collapsed to delivery_unknown, which is never retried and never re-minted
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). voice_post_discord's exit status is discarded into VOICE_HTTP_CODE='000' and routed to record_voice_source_delivery delivery_unknown. delivery_unknown is absent from CLAIMABLE_STATES (voice-health.py:85) and from retryableIntentIds (voice-health-projector.ts), and _open_episode returns the existing episode's existing intent while the episode stays open, so no new intent is minted. No meta-alert fires, and the receipt matches SAFE_ALERT_RECEIPT so the Bridge does not even log. Failure: the host's network drops — exactly the condition that opens the episode — curl exits 7 and the alert is lost for the whole episode. Plan section 4 draws the line at '明确未发送/429可以按既有队列重试'; curl exit 6/7 is 明确未发送 and the evidence is discarded.

advisories.title: Bootstrap startup-spool events are imported only when there is exactly one demand identity
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). readStartupEvents() is invoked only under demandState==='required' && sourceStatus==='available' && identities.length === 1. With zero or two-or-more concurrent voice demands — and now also during the new fail-closed window, which forces identities to [] — wrapper-level startup failures are never imported, never alerted and never archived. The writer caps the spool at 128 files / 1MB and the overflow is swallowed by '|| true', so once saturated, later startup failures are dropped with only stderr. Plan section 4's bootstrap path expects unconditional import keyed on the Bridge's own demand association. Separately, spool/consumed/ has no pruning owner.

advisories.title: createVoiceHealthStartupSpoolReader() is constructed with no root while every sibling in the same call gets FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR, so an isolated Bridge reads and can consume the host's production spool
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). plugin.ts:7215 computes voiceHealthStateRoot from FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR?.trim() || ~/.flywheel and passes it to readExport and the guard; three lines later readStartupEvents: createVoiceHealthStartupSpoolReader() is called with no argument and the reader resolves join(input.homeDir ?? homedir(), '.flywheel', 'voice-startup-spool'), never consulting FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR. scripts/test-deploy.sh:1598 gives a 529 slot Bridge FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR=${state} with no HOME override, so a slot Bridge reads the founder's real spool on every tick. If that slot's own store reports required demand with exactly one identity it wins the .consumer.lock flock, records the production startup failure into the SLOT's health DB, and renames the production document into consumed/ — after which the production Bridge never mints the intent. Honest boundary: the cross-root read is unconditional and certain; the consume branch is reachable but I could not construct a slot run that reaches it, and evidence is archived rather than deleted. The homeDir parameter already exists and is used by the reader's own test.

advisories.title: validateExport's `currentProjection === undefined` guard does not catch the helper's JSON null, so a source with no health row fails every tick
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). Probed against a virgin state root: export returns "currentProjection":null (voice-health.py _current_projection returns None when the health row is absent). validateExport's check `(!raw.hasMore && raw.currentProjection === undefined)` uses strict equality so null passes, then record(exported.currentProjection, ...) throws in BOTH projectView and the Bridge guard — the latter BEFORE the startup_not_ready waiting block. The projector then throws, marks the projection unavailable, logs every tick, and the guard plus the startup-spool import never run. It normally self-heals because record-demand creates the health row (confirmed by probe) and VoiceSessionRuntime.start() fires before the awaited startup tick, so the practical exposure is the startup race plus any host where record-demand can never succeed.

advisories.title: pause() never detaches its abort listener on the timer path, while this PR feeds it a long-lived AbortSignal on every idle poll
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). pause() registers signal.addEventListener('abort', fn, {once:true}) and returns on the timer path WITHOUT removeEventListener; {once:true} only detaches after the event fires, and abort fires once at shutdown. This PR introduced the exposure: pre-PR daemon.ts called options.sleep(idlePollMs) with NO signal (verified against e82193650:daemon.ts:244,309), whereas run() now passes this.sleepController.signal — one AbortController per daemon (daemon.ts:302) — at daemon.ts:326 and :348, and cli.ts:357 wires sleep: pause. One listener is permanently retained per idle poll: 12/min at the FLYWHEEL_VOICE_IDLE_POLL_MS default of 5000, ~17k/day. I verified Node emits NO MaxListenersExceededWarning for AbortSignal at 40 listeners, so the growth is silent. One removeEventListener in the timer path closes it.

advisories.title: claim/renew install the lease from an unvalidated body.leaseTtlMs, so a malformed 2xx produces a NaN deadline that never fences plus a 1ms timer spin
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). This PR rewrote the request layer specifically so a 2xx is not assumed successful and added strict decoding for /desired, but claim (:306), renew (:332) and renewRecovered (:352) still pass body.leaseTtlMs straight into VoiceLease.install, whose only typing is a compile-time generic on a network response. With leaseTtlMs absent or non-numeric, deadlineMs = sentAt + NaN - timeout = NaN (:105); VoiceLease.assert() then evaluates `!active || monoNow() >= NaN` = false and never throws, so the fence that stops two daemons from both believing they hold authority is silently disabled for the session. SessionLifetime.armDeadline re-arms with lease.remainingMs = NaN, which Node coerces to a 1ms delay, producing a ~1000/s re-arm spin. A Number.isSafeInteger guard in install() closes both.

advisories.title: record_delivery has no post-timeout idempotency key, so a worker cannot confirm its own committed write
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). The authorization side is sound — 'sent' requires a matching claim_token, matching binding_digest, intent['channel_id'] == channel_id and snowflake-validated ids, so no fabricated success — but the UPDATE clears claim_token, claimed_at and claim_expires_at. A retry after a 500ms execFile timeout that actually committed returns notification_claim_mismatch, indistinguishable from a genuinely wrong claim. Plan section 3 requires '超时后不能假设未提交：用 ... 重试查询去重记录'. Every other mutating command has such a key.

advisories.title: voice_health_demand_events is retention-protected forever while the consuming cursor is in-memory, so Bridge restarts replay the whole history
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). scripts/lib/fly-2006-retention-tables/teamlead/voice_health_demand_events.json classifies the table protectedCurrentOrReference, which fly-2006-retention-loader.mjs treats as a non-delete category — so the append-only trigger log in the shared production teamlead DB grows one row per voice_sessions insert/delete/state/reason/cancel/ending/ended change, forever. demandCursor is a plain in-memory field reset to 0 on every Bridge restart, and projectVoiceDemand drains one 200-event page per 3s tick, so catch-up costs N/200 x 3s. Mitigated this round: because observedAt is now the Bridge clock rather than a data timestamp, demand_observed_at no longer freezes during catch-up, so the fixed page no longer reads stale for the whole replay window — the unbounded growth and linear catch-up remain.

advisories.title: demandEvent() drops cancelRequested / endingStarted / previousState, so the helper cannot tell a cancelled demand from a dependency failure
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). The trigger records cancel_requested, ending_started, ended and old_state (StateStore.ts:2810-2859) precisely so the helper can distinguish 'user cancelled' from 'system failed it', but the recorder forwards only eventSeq/eventKind/demandId/attemptId/observedAt (+reasonClass for 'failed'). Failure: a founder cancels a meeting, the session goes ending then times out, and voiceHealthReasonClass maps ending_timeout to session_runtime_failed — the helper opens a session_unavailable incident and pages the engineering channel for a user-initiated cancel. Plan section 3 (防止失败后自动消警) requires the cancel fact to be carried into the record.

advisories.title: claim/setState/outbound/receipt failures propagate to the poll path and are recorded as poll_dependency, which a later idle_success closes
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). runOnce() lets bridge.claim() and the lifetime bridge calls throw out to run()'s catch, where pollFailure() records kind:'poll_failed' carrying the diagnostic's operation (claim/state/outbound/receipt). voice-health.py opens a poll_dependency episode for those, and _close_poll_episode closes it on the next idle_success — so a failure to join the room is cleared by an unrelated idle poll, the scope-isolation outcome plan section 3 forbids. Partially mitigated because the demand path independently opens session_unavailable on required->failed and the startup guard covers 'desired' sessions, so this is noise plus premature recovery rather than total blindness.

advisories.title: A failure to report the terminal session state to the Bridge is swallowed with no health observation
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). Both terminal paths wrap bridge.setState in try/catch, set terminalConfirmed=false and only console.error('[voice] session terminal receipt unavailable; recovery state retained'). Before this change the error propagated out of runOnce and was counted by run()'s catch. Now the Bridge round-trip failure produces no poll_failed and no session_failed observation, no episode and no alert — a whole class of bridge_* failures on the terminal path is invisible to the ledger this change exists to build. recover() (daemon.ts:365-413) likewise emits no health observation on the equivalent path.

advisories.title: config_error and invalid receipts retry every 30s forever with no cap, no backoff and no dead-letter transition
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). VoiceHealthAlertDispatcher.drain treats config_error and any unparsable receipt as a retry and calls scheduleRetry with a fixed 30s delay, unbounded. lead-alert.sh returns config_error for permanent conditions (missing helper, failed route preflight, invalid frozen payload), so a misconfigured route spawns /bin/bash lead-alert.sh every 30s for the daemon's lifetime; the Bridge does the same every 60s. claim_notification increments attempt_count but nothing enforces a limit or a dead_lettered transition. meta-alert.sh's 10-minute per-reason debounce bounds the alert noise, but not the process churn or the growing attempt_count.

advisories.title: The new 60s+60s leased-startup bound can fire startup_not_ready while a session is still legitimately inside its 120s founder-presence grace
advisories.detail: NEW this round, arising from the (correct) fix to warming-lease-suppresses-startup-guard. The guard now excuses a leased claimed/warming session only while now - createdAt < STARTUP_NOT_READY_MS + LEASED_STARTUP_GRACE_MS = 120s. But the daemon's own legitimate wait is presenceGraceMs, default 120_000 (config.ts:161), and it begins only after desired->claim->setState warming->session.start(), i.e. roughly createdAt+5..25s — so waitForFounder can legitimately run until createdAt+125..145s. A founder who joins the voice channel more than ~110s after the session row is created therefore gets a session_unavailable / startup_not_ready incident and a Discord alert for a system that then works. It self-heals (the same session reaching live+renew emits session_recovered, which matches the current identity and closes the episode since liveAt > openedAt), so the cost is alert noise rather than a stuck incident, and the chosen bound is already twice as lenient as the plan's stated 60s boundary. Consider deriving the grace from presenceGraceMs, or anchoring the boundary on the desired->claimed transition rather than createdAt.

advisories.title: _restore_demand_marker restores source_status but not the demand_source_unavailable reason_class that idle_success nulls out
advisories.detail: NEW this round; a small residual in the otherwise-correct fix to result-write-erases-demand-source-unavailable. Verified against the real helper: after a fail-closed record-demand (trigger_invalid) the row reads {demandState: unknown, sourceStatus: unavailable, reasonClass: demand_source_unavailable}; after one ordinary idle_success it reads {demandState: unknown, sourceStatus: unavailable, reasonClass: None}. The two fields the projector actually derives status from (sourceStatus, demandState) are now correctly preserved — which is why the page behaviour is right — but the recorded fault class is still erased by idle_success's `reason_class = NULL`, so the health row loses the diagnostic that says WHY the source is unavailable. Restoring reason_class alongside source_status in _restore_demand_marker would make the marker whole.

advisories.title: The voice-health tick is the only projector awaited ahead of gatePoller.start(); bounded, but an unnecessary boot dependency
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). Bounded and not a real availability risk, per measurement. Ceiling is ~265 sequential helper calls (two drains of <=32 pages, 1 evaluate, <=128 spool record-startup, <=8 waiting record-startup), each capped by execFile timeout: 500 plus <=128 lock acquisitions at readyTimeoutMs: 500 — but that requires all 265 calls to SUCCEED just under 500ms, since any rejection short-circuits run(). No hang risk: voice-health.py has zero hits for subprocess|Popen|os.system|os.fork. Measured ~45ms/call, so a typical boot is ~0.15s and a full 128-event spool ~6-12s. Flagged only because the two sibling projectors constructed just above live solely in the async 3s poller, whose rejections GatePoller already catches and logs; dropping the pre-start await costs at most one poll cycle of freshness.

advisories.title: The TypeScript route/bindingDigest module has zero production importers
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). A repo-wide grep for 'voice-health-alert-route' outside dist finds exactly one importer: packages/teamlead/src/__tests__/voice-health-alert-delivery.test.ts. Production route resolution happens entirely in scripts/lead-alert.sh via node scripts/shuttle-route-bindings.mjs, and the bindingDigest persisted and revalidated by the helper comes from that shell path — not from resolveVoiceHealthAlertRoute, which computes a different digest. The repo carries two independent definitions of the same contract, only one of which ships. Coverage of the shipped path is not missing (scripts/__tests__/voice-health-alert-route.test.sh exercises the real shell sender and passes), so the cost is drift risk plus a TS test that looks like production routing coverage but is not.

advisories.title: main() reads stdin unconditionally for every subcommand, so any caller that does not close stdin hangs forever with no deadline
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred as 已记录). `payload = _read_payload()` runs before the command dispatch, so even `init` — which then requires the payload to be None or {} — blocks on an open stdin. PROVEN: `timeout 4 python3 scripts/lib/voice-health.py --state-root $TMP init < <(sleep 30)` exits 124 (hung), while the same command with `</dev/null` exits 0. The helper has no internal deadline. Production callers are safe (the TS clients call child.stdin.end() and bound with timeout: 500; lead-alert.sh pipes via printf which closes stdin), but this already cost the implementer debugging time on macOS, and any future runbook, cron or QA script invoking the helper without redirecting stdin will hang indefinitely. Read stdin only for the commands that take a payload, or only when it is not a TTY.

advisories.title: reportFatalStartupFailure discards the error entirely, leaving zero diagnostic for a daemon that will not start
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). The parameter is named _error and the log line is the constant '[voice] fatal reasonClass=startup_not_ready operation=startup'; the spool record carries only the reasonClass. This follows plan section 3's rule that raw Error.message must not reach stderr, and package-onboard-smoke.test.sh asserts the exact string. The cost is that 'voice will not start' — the originating FLY-2693 symptom — produces no locally recoverable detail anywhere. A bounded closed-vocabulary classifier (e.g. mapping the known config errors to startup_config_invalid) would keep the sanitization and restore triage.

advisories.title: validateVoiceBridgeUrl hard-fails any non-loopback BRIDGE_URL with no allowlist
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). loadVoiceDaemonConfig throws voice_bridge_url_invalid for any host that is not localhost, [::1] or 127.x.x.x, which the wrapper turns into voice_config_invalid and exit 0. Plan section 2 said '生产默认loopback' and '跨主机部署如存在，按现有可信配置明确allowlist'; no allowlist was implemented, so this is an unannounced hard break for any host configuring a non-loopback Bridge. ::ffff:127.0.0.1 is also unmatched.

advisories.title: The voice alert lane silently inherits SHUTTLE_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE as a permission-preflight override
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). VOICE_HEALTH_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE:-${SHUTTLE_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE:-} means a stale or leaked SHUTTLE_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE in the environment also replaces the real Discord VIEW_CHANNEL/SEND_MESSAGES preflight for voice alerts (shuttle-route-bindings.mjs:301-309). A QA harness that exports it and forgets to unset it downgrades a second production lane's sender check with no signal.

advisories.title: The frozen-payload openedAt gate is prefix-only while every sibling field is fully anchored
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (Lead-deferred). test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T") has no end anchor, and the value is interpolated into the Discord BODY. Not exploitable today — the writer validates via _parse_timestamp, jq -n --arg prevents payload injection, and allowed_mentions:{parse:[]} blocks pings — but it is the one unanchored field in an otherwise closed-vocabulary gate. Related latent fragility: jq errors with exit 5 on `null | test(...)`, so any _open_episode call site leaving health.operation NULL would make its alert permanently undeliverable; I re-checked the call sites and each sets operation first, so this is latent only.

advisories.title: The demand digest omits project_name and meeting_id, and neither column is in the trigger's UPDATE OF list
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED, and deliberate per follow-ups.md ('无关字段更新不改变 revision/digest'). Recording the residual consequence: digestRows carries session_id/state/cancel/ending/ended/reasonClass while demandIdentities also carries projectId and meetingId, and voice_health_demand_sessions_update fires only on state, reason, cancel_requested_at, ending_started_at, ended_at — so an identity-only change (e.g. meeting_id backfilled) produces no event and no digest change, and the helper keeps stale identities, which record_result's session_failed path uses for identity_matches.
